research_question: Can cooperative global-budget arbitration across staggered multi-camera YOLO26n streams (N=4 K=1 and N=8 K=2, 25% duty cycle) reduce mean and peak phys_footprint proportionally to active duty cycle on macOS 16 KiB pages while preserving p99 latency and bit-exact FP32 outputs?
hypothesis: Shedding oldest-idle streams synchronously at burst handoff via GlobalBudgetArbiter reduces mean phys_footprint by >=40% vs BFC/retain, eliminates the idle-timer lag of per-stream auto-idle reclamation, and keeps p99 latency within 10% of retain with max_abs_error == 0.
acceptance_gates: 1) max_abs_error == 0 across all 45 runs; 2) pool_coop mean phys_footprint <= 0.60x pool_retain and bfc for N=4 K=1 and N=8 K=2; 3) pool_coop p99 latency <= 1.10x pool_retain; 4) validate_run.py --require-protocol --min-trials 5 passes.
